subject: Cygnus: connectivity anomaly — DNS/VPC handoff causing spike in 5xx and latency (exec action)
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@cygnus.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Sudden error surge and latency from our east-us customers

Marissa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and 300-900ms added tail latency for inference calls coming from our east-us region starting ~03:00 UTC today. This correlates with a spike in failed handshakes and retry storms on our side. Our engineers see frequent NXDOMAIN responses from the resolver chain intermittently and timeouts at the proxy layer.

Can Redwood confirm if there were any routing or peering changes on your end? We rely on the vpc-peering path to your ingress, and this is impacting our checkout flow. We're getting executive questions and need a quick mitigation plan.

Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform, Cygnus AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@cygnus.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 09:41:12 -08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden error surge and latency from our east-us customers

Elena — thanks for the heads up. We're pulling traces now. Initial check: no planned peering maintenance on Redwood's side during that window. Rishi is running cross-region traceroutes and we're validating our DNS resolvers.

Action items for now:
- Rishi: gather traceroutes + tcpdump from the affected POPs (ETA 45m)
- Stephanie: verify whether our edge proxy pool experienced a config rollout at 02:30–04:00 UTC
- Cygnus Ops: can you attach your resolver dig output and any load balancer logs you have for 02:00–04:30 UTC?

I'll escalate to Ops Execs if we find a peering or firewall policy overlap. We're prepared to fail traffic to east-us-2 to a backup path if needed, but want to validate DNS handoff first.

-marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2027 06:02:03 -08:00
Subject: Traces + packet captures from edge POPs (attached)

Attaching raw traceroute and sample pcap (excerpts) from two affected POPs in us-east. Observations:
- Intermittent 100–500ms latency jumps on the peering hop 10.200.45.1 -> 198.51.100.13 with packet retransmits
- Several queries to customer resolvers returning SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN before succeeding after retry (~2s)
- Edge proxy occasionally returning 502 with upstream handshake failure at TLS layer (SNI mismatches seen in ~4% of sampled reqs)

Likely candidates: transient peering congestion or intermittent NAT/firewall that silently drops packets causing TCP/TLS handshake retries.

Files attached: cygnus-traceroute-20271212.txt, cygnus-packet-capture-snippet.pcap.txt

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2027 10:22:45 -08:00
Subject: RE: Traces + packet captures from edge POPs (attached)

Marissa / team,

We've attached our dig outputs for the timeframe (cygnus-dns-dig-ttl-20271213.txt). Notable: our primary resolver estate returned repeated SERVFAILs towards one of Redwood's authoritative caches (auth-east-1.redwood.internal) between 02:05–02:28 UTC. After 02:28 traffic to that cache dropped off and queries timed out before falling back to another cache — causing client retries.

We also noticed an increase in SYN retransmits originating from Redwood's peer ASN to one of our NAT gateways. We're sharing logs via the secure folder.

Elena
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 08:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Config audit: no rollout, but proxy health probes saw elevated error rates

Quick update from proxy/edge team: there was no config rollout during the window. However the health-check system saw probe failures to the upstream caches for ~22 minutes and briefly marked a subset (~8%) of the edge proxy pool as unhealthy which caused additional routing churn. We've queued a temporary remediation: extend probe timeout and exclude the one problematic cache from the health checks while we investigate.

Proposed mitigation (immediate):
- Set probe timeout from 1s -> 3s for edge pool A (affects ~9 POPs)
- Add manual exception to avoid draining when transient SERVFAIL observed
- Open a coordinated ticket with the network partner at partner ASN (cc: Jason Kline) to validate BGP/peering flaps during the 02:00–03:00 UTC window

If approved, I'll roll the probe-timeout change across affected POPs now (5-10 min rollout).

-stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal SRE, Edge Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@cygnus.ai>, Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Kline <jkline@cloud-partner.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 14:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec sync and proposed rollback/mitigation plan

Team — summary for execs and next steps (drafting a one-page exec brief, attached):
- Impact: Cygnus reported sustained 5xx spike and elevated latencies for east-us traffic between 02:00–04:30 UTC on 2027-12-11. Peak error rate reached ~6.3% for inference endpoints; customer reported checkout failures.
- Root-candidate signals: intermittent DNS SERVFAIL from Redwood auth cache, peering hop packet loss/retransmits, and edge proxy health-probe churn causing partial pool drains. No config rollouts on Redwood side during window.

Immediate mitigations (approved by Edge Ops):
1) Apply probe-timeout increase (Stephanie) — rolling now (ETA 10m).
2) Temporarily remove problematic cache from probe set and failover to secondary caches (ETA 20m).
3) Work with partner ASN (Jason) to confirm historic BGP adj-flaps and filter anomalies (Jason: please share your findings).
4) If client-facing impact persists >1h after mitigations, fail traffic from east-us to backup egress path (us-east-2) and open customer-facing incident update.

Request from Cygnus: an exec-level summary they can share with their leadership. I'm attaching a short PDF brief and will prepare a 5-minute slide for the post-mortem.

Marissa
From: Elena Torres <elena@cygnus.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Cygnus Ops <ops@cygnus.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Jason Kline <jkline@cloud-partner.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Exec sync and proposed rollback/mitigation plan

Marissa — thank you for the quick coordination and the exec brief. The probe-timeout change reduced the observed 5xx from 6.3% -> 1.1% in our sampling within 18 minutes, and tail latency 95p improved by ~180ms. We're good to postpone the path failover for now, but Cygnus leadership wants a joint RCA and a timeline for permanent fixes (BGP flaps / upstream NAT behavior).

Could we schedule a 30-min exec review (post-mortem + mitigating SLO guardrails) for Friday 11:00 PT? I'll invite our CTO.

—Elena
